messages.author: c0eeebc5f5a22d1e
messages.subject: Problems running radon example from ARM
parts:
Hi there,


I am trying to learn Stan, and run an example from Chapter 17 of Gelman & Hill (2006). I am running example 17.1_radon_wishart, from

https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/blob/master/ARM/Ch.17/17.1_radon_wishart.stan

However, when I run it, I get a number of errors/warnings:

For each chain:                                                                 

Exception thrown at line 39: wishart_log: LDLT_Factor of random variable is not positive definite. count=8

Warning messages:

1: In readLines(file, warn = TRUE) :

 incomplete final line found on '/path/to/stan/17.1_radon_wishart.stan'

2: There were 170 divergent transitions after warmup. Increasing adapt_delta above 0.8 may help. See

http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#divergent-transitions-after-warmup

3: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems


I also receive the warnings that are pasted at the bottom of this message. I examine the pairs plot and there are divergent transitions above and below the diagonal. I have attached the files I am running, however note these are just copy/pasted from github.


It seems strange that an example problem would give such errors, so I must be doing something wrong! Help would be greatly appreciated.


I have R version 3.3.2 (2016-10-31), rstan_2.14.1 and RStudio Version 1.0.44 on OS Sierra. 

Thanks and regards, Chris

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problems running radon example from ARM
parts:
That models' not fitting well (the divergence warnings are real, but
the rest of it's just compiler stuff we haven't been able to silence in
R.

We need to go through and fix all those example models which
were just translated directly from the book (and often didn't work in BUGS,
either!). That's on the agenda this year.

For multivariate hierarchical priors, we strongly recommend the
Cholesky parameterization scaled correlation matrices as described
in the manual chapter on regression. To make Wishart efficient and
robust, we'd need to have a Cholesky factor parameterization, which
may be coming soon.

- Bob

Jonah
